blocks.task_summary: Find the indefinite integral of (x^2 - 5) e^x dx.
method_path: Apply integration by parts with u = x^2 - 5, dv = e^x dx
Apply integration by parts a second time to the resulting integral
accepted_alternatives: Integration by parts with u = e^x, dv = (x^2 - 5) dx, then integrate by parts again

evidence.basis: attempt to use integration by parts (M1); (x^2 - 5) e^x - ∫ e^x (2x) dx OR ... A1; attempt to use integration by parts a second time (M1); ... A1; (x^2 - 5) e^x - (2x e^x - 2 e^x) (A1); (x^2 - 2x - 3) e^x + c OR ... A1

blocks.task_summary: Solve the differential equation dy/dx + y = x^2 - 5 and show the solution can be expressed as y = x^2 - 2x - 3 + C e^{-x}.
method_path: Rearrange to standard form dy/dx + y = x^2 - 5
Find integrating factor e^{∫ 1 dx} = e^x
Multiply both sides by e^x and recognize left side as derivative of e^x y
Integrate both sides using result from part (a)
Solve for y to obtain y = x^2 - 2x - 3 + C e^{-x}

evidence.basis: rearranging to dy/dx + y = x^2 - 5 AND attempt to find integrating factor (M1); e^{∫ 1 dx} = e^x (seen anywhere) A1; e^x dy/dx + e^x y = e^x (x^2 - 5) ... M1; e^x y = (x^2 - 2x - 3) e^x + C OR ... A1; y = x^2 - 2x - 3 + C e^{-x} AG

blocks.task_summary: Sketch the particular solution passing through (-3, 2) for -4 ≤ x ≤ 4, labelling local maximum and minimum points.
method_path: Substitute x = -3, y = 2 into general solution to find C
Obtain particular solution y = x^2 - 2x - 3 - 0.498 e^{-x} (or equivalent)
Sketch curve with correct shape, x-intercepts, local maximum at (-2.70, 2.28), local minimum at (0.899, -4.19), domain -4 ≤ x ≤ 4

evidence.basis: substituting x = -3, y = 2 into y = x^2 - 2x - 3 + C e^{-x} (M1); C = -0.497870... (= -10 e^{-3}) A1; y = x^2 - 2x - 3 - 0.498 e^{-x} (accept y = x^2 - 2x - 3 - 10 e^{-x-3}) A1A1A1; Note: A1 for approximately correct shape AND x-intercepts in approximately correct place; A1 for maximum in approximately correct position and labelled (-2.70, 2.28) AND minimum in approximately correct position and labelled (0.899, -4.19); A1 for domain.

blocks.task_summary: Show that all tangents at x = -3 to the family of solution curves intersect at a common point, and state its coordinates.
method_path: Substitute x = -3 into dy/dx = x^2 - 5 - y to find gradient in terms of y-coordinate
Write equations of tangents at (-3, p) and (-3, q)
Solve the two tangent equations simultaneously to find intersection point
Show intersection point is (-2, 4) independent of p and q

evidence.basis: substituting -3 and p OR -3 and q into dy/dx (M1); gradient of tangent at (-3, p) is 4 - p and at (-3, q) is 4 - q; finding equation of tangents (M1); y - p = (4 - p)(x + 3) AND y - q = (4 - q)(x + 3) A1; solving their equations simultaneously (M1); ... x + 3 = 1 (since p ≠ q) x = -2 A1; y - p = 4 - p OR y - q = 4 - q y = 4 A1; hence all tangents intersect at (-2, 4) AG
